overview.label: Overview
overview.desc: Version, updates and what's in it

health.label: Health
health.desc: Missing files and what needs fixing

logs.label: Logs
logs.desc: What the server has been doing

activity.title: Activity
activity.description: Sign-ins, and what's being read, watched and listened to, on every account.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: How Plinthio looks for everyone: the server's defaults, its name, and your own CSS. Changes save as you make them.

personalize.label: Let people personalize
personalize.desc: Each person can pick their own colour, navigation, width and pause screen in Settings → Appearance. Turn off to use the server's look for everyone.

cards.accent: The highlight colour on buttons, badges and the current tab.
cards.pageWidth: How wide pages get on a big screen.
cards.pauseScreen: What appears after a couple of seconds paused; it fades when someone moves the mouse or touches the screen. Cast, crew and facts come from TMDB when a key is set.

branding.title: Name and sign-in notice
branding.desc: Your server's name, and an optional notice on the sign-in page.

css.title: Custom CSS
css.desc: Your own style rules, added to every page for everyone. Try them here first; they go live when you save.

backups.title: Backups
backups.description: Snapshots of the database: accounts, everyone's progress, bookmarks, highlights and notes, ratings, lists, libraries and metadata. Not your media files. A snapshot is also taken before every upgrade, and the newest five of those are always kept.

destination.label: Also copy backups to
destination.why: /config/backups is on the same disk as the server. A copy on another drive, a NAS or a synced cloud folder survives that disk failing.
destination.writableFree: The server can write there · {free} free.
destination.sameDisk: It's on the same disk as the server's data, so it guards against mistakes but not a failed disk. A folder on another drive is better.
destination.otherDisk: It's on a different disk from the server's data.
destination.hint: A folder as the server sees it. In Docker: anywhere under {media} that isn't read-only, or another drive mounted at {backups} (Docs → Backups & Data Safety).
destination.copyFiles: Also copy profile pictures, covers, the sign-in key and HTTPS certificates

backups.savedCopying: Saved. The backups you have are being copied to {path}.
backups.copyFailed: Copying to {path} failed: {error}. It's tried again every 15 minutes.
backups.empty: No backups yet. Turn on automatic backups or back up now.
backups.couldNotSnapshot: Could not make a snapshot. The browser console has the details.
backups.couldNotDownload: Could not download that backup. The browser console has the details.
backups.deleteMessage: Delete the backup from {date}? This can't be undone.

features.title: Features
features.description: What's switched on for everyone on this server. Changes save as you make them.

shelfViews.title: Shelf views
shelfViews.desc: Alphabetical and Creator are always there. Turning a folder view off hides it for everyone.

diskFolder.label: Disk folders
diskFolder.desc: Browse by the folders on the server.

customFolder.label: Custom folders
customFolder.desc: People's own in-app folders, with an Unorganized catch-all.

ratings.title: Ratings
ratings.desc: Which ratings appear. One turned off is hidden everywhere, and the server stops sending it.

personal.label: Personal ratings
personal.desc: Each person can give 1–5 stars, and sees their own.

community.label: {name} ratings
community.desc: The average from everyone on this server.

external.label: World ratings (TMDB)
external.desc: TMDB's score for movies, shows and anime. Needs a TMDB key.

missingFilms.label: Show missing films in collections
missingFilms.desc: A collection like Shrek or Star Wars also lists the films you don't have, greyed out with a Request button. They never appear on the Movies shelf. Needs a TMDB key.

watchParties.label: Watch parties
watchParties.desc: A Watch Together button on movies and episodes: watch in sync from different places, with chat. Content limits still apply to everyone in a party. Friends away from home need to be able to reach this server (see Network). Turning it off ends any party in progress.

kids.title: Kids Mode
kids.description: Kids accounts see only what's switched on here. Make an account a kids account in Users.

libraries.title: Whole libraries
libraries.desc: Everything in these libraries, now and later.

titles.title: Single series and titles
titles.desc: Add more from any series or title page with its {button} button.

kids.couldNotRemove: Could not remove it from Kids Mode

libraries.title: Libraries
libraries.description: The folders Plinthio reads your media from. It never changes your files.
libraries.empty: No libraries yet. Add one to point Plinthio at a folder of media.

autoScan.title: Automatic scanning
autoScan.desc: Picks up media added to your library folders without anyone pressing Scan.

scheduled.label: Re-scan on a schedule
scheduled.desc: The dependable one: works on network shares and mounts that report no changes.

autoScan.timesHint: In the server's time zone. If the server was off at a set time, it scans once when it's back.

watch.label: Watch folders for changes
watch.desc: Scans about 30 seconds after a file appears, where the filesystem reports it. Works with or without the schedule.

autoScan.manual: Automatic scanning is off. New media won't show up until an admin presses Scan on a library.
autoScan.noSchedule: Without a schedule, changes on network shares or mounts that send no file events won't be noticed until you press Scan.
autoScan.noTimes: No times set, so the schedule never runs. Add a time, or switch to regular intervals.

addDialog.title: Add a library
addDialog.folderHint: As the server sees it. In Docker, your media is mounted at {path}.
addDialog.name: Name

libraries.deleteMessage: Delete "{name}"? Your files aren't touched, and progress and bookmarks come back if you add the same folder again. Its titles, covers and details are removed until it's scanned again.

liveTv.title: Live TV
liveTv.description: Live channels with a programme guide, from public lists or your own playlists. Changes save as you make them.

switch.label: Live TV
switch.desc: Adds a Live TV page with channels and a programme guide for everyone on this server. Off by default; turning it off hides Live TV everywhere, but keeps your lists and choices here.

liveTv.publicNote: Channels come from public sources on the internet. Some may be offline, break now and then, or only play in certain countries. Adult channels are never added.
liveTv.responsibility: You choose which channels to add, and you're responsible for having the right to watch them where you are. Plinthio doesn't host, check or endorse any channel.

sources.title: Channel lists
sources.desc: Each list is reloaded every 12 hours while Live TV is on, along with its programme guide.
sources.empty: No channels yet. Add a ready-made list or your own playlist to get started.

removeMessage.one: Remove {name}? Its {number} channel goes too, along with whether it was hidden or allowed for kids.
removeMessage.other: Remove {name}? Its {number} channels go too, along with which were hidden or allowed for kids.

sources.offHint: Live TV is switched off, so nobody sees these channels yet. You can get them ready first.
sources.couldNotLoad: Could not load the channel lists

editDialog.title: Edit channel list
editDialog.guideHint: Leave empty to use the guide the playlist names, if it has one.

public.intro: Free channels from the public iptv-org lists, updated daily. Pick one or more; each is added as its own list.
public.note: These channels come from public sources, so some may be offline or only play in certain countries. Adult channels are never added.
public.couldNotLoad: Could not load the public lists

own.name: Name
own.playlistHint: An address the server can reach. Channels that stream in HLS (.m3u8) play; others are listed as not playable.
own.guideHint: Leave empty to use the guide the playlist names, if it has one. Compressed .xml.gz files work too.

acknowledge.title: Before you add public channels

points.links: Public lists are links to third-party streams. Plinthio doesn't host, check or vouch for any of them.
points.licensing: Some channels only play in certain countries (region-locked), and some may not be licensed where you are.
points.yourCall: Only add channels you're allowed to watch. Which channels you add is up to you, and so is the responsibility for them.

acknowledge.couldNotSave: Could not save that, try again

filters.title: Choose what to show
filters.desc: Hide whole sets of channels at once. These choices stay when the lists reload, and new channels that match are hidden too. To keep one channel from a hidden set, use Always show under Channels.
filters.noChannels: No playable channels yet. Counts appear here once a list has loaded.

desc.one: {number} channel is marked Geo-blocked: it only plays in certain countries and usually fails everywhere else.
desc.other: {number} channels are marked Geo-blocked: they only play in certain countries and usually fail everywhere else.

hints.groups: Categories come from the lists themselves. A channel in several categories is hidden when any of them is hidden.
hints.languages: A channel in several languages is hidden only when all of them are hidden. Channels with no language listed aren't affected.
hints.countries: The country a channel comes from. Channels with no country listed aren't affected.
hints.hosts: Some public channels aren't streamed by the broadcaster but re-routed through a third-party service. Hiding a host drops all of its channels. Plinthio hides one such service, jmp2.uk, until you show it; only do that if you're sure you may watch those channels.

filters.tip: Tip: to keep only a few, press Hide all, then switch on the ones you want.

empty.groups: None of the channels has a category.
empty.languages: None of the channels has a language listed.
empty.countries: None of the channels has a country listed.

channels.title: Channels
channels.desc: Hide the ones you don't want, or press the pencil to give one its own number, name or logo. Kids accounts see only the channels allowed for kids here or in a line-up that allows kids, and none are allowed until you pick them.
channels.alwaysShowHint: Show even when a filter under Choose what to show hides it
channels.followFiltersHint: Stop always showing, so the filters apply again

badges.geoBlockedHint: Marked as only playing in certain countries
badges.unsupportedHint: Not an HLS stream, so it isn't offered to anyone
badges.filteredHint: Hidden by Choose what to show ({reasons}). Use Always show to keep this channel anyway.
badges.pinnedHint: Always shown, whatever the filters say. Press again to let the filters decide.
badges.pinnedOverHint: Always shown, even though a filter hides {reasons}. Press again to let the filters decide.
badges.offlineHint: Didn't play in its last two checks (last checked {date})

channels.empty: No channels yet. They appear here once a list has loaded.
channels.editAria: Edit number, name and logo of {name}

health.title: Channel health
health.desc: Public channels come and go. Plinthio checks a few at a time in the background to find the ones that have stopped working. Each check only asks the stream for its first couple of kilobytes, so nothing is played or converted and the server hardly notices.

enabled.label: Check channels in the background
enabled.desc: About 20 channels every 10 minutes while Live TV is on, so each channel is looked at roughly once a day.

hideOffline.label: Hide offline channels
hideOffline.desc: A channel that fails two checks in a row is hidden from viewers. It's checked again about once a day and comes back on its own once it plays.

health.pace: Channels are checked a few at a time; Check now on a channel looks straight away.
health.paused: Background checks are off, so these counts stay as they are.

editChannel.title: Edit channel
editChannel.numberHint: 1 to 9999, each used once. Viewers can type it to jump to this channel. Channels without a number follow on after your highest one.
editChannel.numberInvalid: Use a whole number from 1 to 9999.
editChannel.name: Name
editChannel.nameHint: Leave empty to use the list's name: {name}
editChannel.logoHint: A link to a picture (http or https). Leave empty to use the list's own logo. The new logo shows once saved.
editChannel.checkHint: See whether this channel plays right now. A channel is marked offline only after two failed checks in a row.

lineups.title: Line-ups
lineups.desc: Make your own sets of channels, such as News, Sport or For the kids, in the order you like. Each line-up is a tab on the Live TV page, in the order shown here.
lineups.empty: No line-ups yet. Viewers see all channels by category until you make one.
lineups.footer: In a line-up, viewers still don't see channels you've hidden or that are offline, and the filters still apply unless a channel is set to Always show.
lineups.name: Name
lineups.nameHint: Shown to viewers as the tab's name.

kids.label: Allow for kids
kids.desc: Kids accounts may watch every channel in this line-up, as well as the channels allowed for kids one by one.

lineups.deleteMessage: Delete {name}? Its channels stay where they are; only the line-up goes.
lineups.couldNotLoadChannels: Could not load this line-up's channels

editor.subtitle: Changes save as you make them
editor.empty: No channels in this line-up yet.
editor.searchHint: Type part of a channel's name.

moreResults.one: {number} more match; type more to narrow it down.
moreResults.other: {number} more matches; type more to narrow it down.

editor.nothingNew: Every channel from that category is already here.

logs.title: Logs
logs.description: Scans, errors and what the server has been doing, newest first.
logs.clearMessage: Delete every log entry from the database?

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Where posters, descriptions, cast and ratings come from, and tidying titles that came in from file names.

tmdb.title: TMDB key
tmdb.descBuiltIn: Movies, shows and anime get their details from TMDB, using the key built into Plinthio. You can paste your own TMDB key to use it instead. Manga (MangaDex) and books (Google Books, Open Library) need nothing.
tmdb.descNeedsKey: Movies, shows and anime get their details from TMDB, which needs a free key. Manga (MangaDex) and books (Google Books, Open Library) need nothing.
tmdb.placeholderReplace: Paste a new key to replace it
tmdb.placeholderToken: Paste your TMDB API Read Access Token
tmdb.attribution: This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
tmdb.removeMessage: Movies, shows and anime stop getting new posters, details and world ratings until a key is added again.

overview.title: Overview
overview.description: This server at a glance: its version, what's in it and who uses it.
overview.upToDateCheckFailed: You're up to date (last check failed — offline?).

playback.title: Playback
playback.description: How video reaches people's screens, and the clip that can play before it.

hwaccel.title: Hardware acceleration
hwaccel.desc: Plinthio plays files as they are whenever the browser can, and only converts what it can't. A graphics chip makes converting far cheaper.
hwaccel.testHint: Test runs a short real conversion: ffmpeg listing an encoder doesn't prove the driver under it works.
hwaccel.howItWorks: How playback works, and setting up a graphics chip

direct.title: Direct play and direct stream:
direct.text: video the browser can decode (H.264, or HEVC in Chrome, Edge, Vivaldi and Safari) is sent untouched, up to 4K, even from MKV files. Only audio it can't play (EAC3, Atmos, DTS) is converted, to AAC.

browser.title: The browser's side:
browser.text: for 4K, check the browser decodes video in hardware ({page} → Video Decode: Hardware accelerated).

docker.title: Intel Quick Sync and VAAPI in Docker:
docker.text: pass {dri} through under {devices}, and add the host's {render} group ID under {groupAdd}.

small.title: Small machines:
small.text: converting on the CPU is held to two threads at the fastest preset, and preview thumbnails are made separately, so a mini PC doesn't overheat.

intro.title: Opening sequence
intro.desc: A short clip played full-screen when someone presses Play on a movie or episode. Never before autoplayed episodes, trailers or watch parties, and anyone can skip it.
intro.builtIn: Plinthio's built-in clip. Replace it with your own:
intro.requirements: MP4 (H.264), 1–10 seconds, up to 20 MB. 1080p at about 8 Mbps is plenty.
intro.offUntil: Off until you turn it on.
intro.tooBig: That file is over 20 MB. Export it shorter or at a lower bitrate.
intro.removeMessage: Remove your clip and go back to Plinthio's built-in opening sequence?

users.title: Users
users.description: Everyone who can sign in to this server. There's no self sign-up: accounts are made here.

viewer.label: Viewer
viewer.desc: Browses, reads, watches and listens; tracks their own progress.

editor.label: Editor
editor.desc: Also fixes shared titles, covers and details.

admin.label: Admin
admin.desc: Everything, including libraries, users and this page.

addDialog.title: Add a user
addDialog.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. They can change it in Settings → Security.

remote.label: Can use Plinthio away from home
remote.desc: When the server allows outside access (Network). Off: only at home and over Tailscale.

kidsAccount.label: Kids account
kidsAccount.desc: Sees only what's switched on in Kids Mode.

users.twoFactorHelp: Lost their phone and backup codes? Reset it so they can sign in with their password and set it up again.
users.allowUnrated: Also show titles that haven't been rated. Off is strict: only rated titles at or under the limit.
users.ratingsHint: Ratings are set on each series or title.
users.newPasswordHint: At least 8 characters. Setting one signs them out everywhere.

badges.twoFactorTitle: Signs in with a code from an authenticator app too
badges.homeOnlyTitle: Can only use Plinthio from the home network

users.passwordTooShort: The new password needs at least 8 characters.
users.resetMessage: {name} will be signed out everywhere, can then sign in with just their password, and can set two-factor up again in Settings → Security.
users.deleteMessage: Delete {name}? Their progress, bookmarks, highlights, lists and ratings go with them.

health.title: Health
health.description: What needs attention across your libraries.
health.unreachable: Folder not reachable — check the drive is mounted and the Docker volume is mapped. Items stay in the catalog until it's back.

missing.title: Missing files
missing.hint: Gone from disk. Deleted them on purpose to free space? Keep them as history: they stay on their title page, greyed, with everyone's progress. Otherwise they're kept hidden for now (a drive can be briefly unavailable) and come back on their own if the files return; remove them for good once you're sure.

offloaded.title: Offloaded (kept as history)
offloaded.hint: Removed to free space and kept as history: hidden from shelves and search, shown greyed on their title page with everyone's progress. If the files come back, they're restored by themselves.

duplicates.title: Likely duplicates
duplicates.hint: Same title and exact same file size — usually the same file in two folders or libraries.

clashes.title: Volume / episode clashes
clashes.hint: Different files that both claim the same volume or episode number in a series. Usually a misnamed file.

metadata.title: Missing artwork or metadata
metadata.hint: {noCover} without cover art, {noAuthor} books/manga/audiobooks without an author, {noDescription} without a description. Fix them in the Metadata tab.

unrated.title: Unrated titles
unrated.hint: Titles with no age rating on themselves or their series. Only matters if you use content limits for some users — rate series from their series sheet, single titles from the metadata editor.

transcode.title: Recent playback encode failures
transcode.hint: ffmpeg errors while preparing video. Often a hardware-acceleration driver problem — try Admin → Playback → Test.

health.couldNotRun: Could not run the health check

keepMessage.one: {label} will stay on its title page, greyed, with everyone's progress, but can't be played. If the files come back, it's restored by itself.
keepMessage.other: {label} will stay on their title page, greyed, with everyone's progress, but can't be played. If the files come back, they're restored by themselves.

health.couldNotKeep: Could not keep those as history
health.removeMessage: Remove {name} from the catalog? Progress and ratings are kept in the database and re-attach if the same files are ever scanned again, but nothing shows it until then.

removeMissingMessage.one: Remove {count} missing title from the catalog for good? Anything whose file has come back is kept, and so is anything kept as history. Reading progress and ratings are kept too, and re-attach if the same files are ever scanned again.
removeMissingMessage.other: Remove {count} missing titles from the catalog for good? Anything whose file has come back is kept, and so is anything kept as history. Reading progress and ratings are kept too, and re-attach if the same files are ever scanned again.

removedSkipped.one: Removed {count} title ({skipped} kept — their files are back).
removedSkipped.other: Removed {count} titles ({skipped} kept — their files are back).

health.scanComplete: Scan of "{name}" complete: {added} added, {updated} updated, {removed} removed.

stillOnDisk.one: {count} still on disk: delete it to free the space.
stillOnDisk.other: {count} still on disk: delete them to free the space.
